name: Open Frontier Curriculum Foundational Doctrine
formal_descriptor: An open, adversarially maintained civilizational reference architecture for lifelong human formation under conditions of abundant machine intelligence.
telos: To help human beings inherit deeply, understand first principles, judge independently, create with taste, act competently, relate humanely, steward wisely, and continue learning throughout life.
design_objective: Form people capable of authorship and stewardship of their lives, relationships, work, institutions, culture, technology, and shared future while using increasingly capable AI as leverage without allowing educational dependence to erase human agency.
anti_objectives: Do not optimize primarily for tasks that current AI cannot perform; that frontier moves too quickly.
Do not reduce education to employability, credentialing, test performance, productivity, or AI complementarity.
Do not treat encyclopedic coverage as equivalent to formation.
Do not preserve a canon merely because it is inherited, or abandon inheritance merely because it is inherited.
Do not assume every consequential AI output can be personally re-derived by one human under superhuman capability regimes.
Do not confuse autonomy with isolation: human agency is embodied, relational, institutional, and intergenerational.
Do not promise immunity from tragedy, perfect prediction, maximum potential, happiness, wealth, virtue, or success.

axioms.title: Human beings are ends, not merely production inputs
axioms.rule: Education must remain intelligible even if human labor ceases to be economically scarce.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Preserve meaning, culture, relationships, citizenship, health, craft, judgment and stewardship as intrinsic educational purposes.

axioms.title: Machine capability does not determine legitimate human ends
axioms.rule: Greater predictive or generative power cannot by itself settle what should be valued, permitted, distributed, protected, loved or built.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Philosophy, Human Worlds, civic judgment and value conflict remain foundational even under superhuman advice.

axioms.title: Human authorship requires internal models
axioms.rule: A person cannot meaningfully choose, question or supervise what they cannot conceptually represent at all.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Maintain an unaided internalization floor in language, mathematics, science, history, philosophy, institutions, health, computing and culture.

axioms.title: Knowledge is distributed and finite minds must collaborate
axioms.rule: No individual can personally contain or verify all consequential knowledge.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Teach source ecology, expertise navigation, division of cognitive labor, institutions of knowledge, AI delegation and layered assurance.

axioms.title: Reality is not generated by the model
axioms.rule: Physical, biological, social and institutional reality can resist elegant abstractions and synthetic consensus.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Require experiments, field observation, primary evidence, users, physical artifacts, operations, history and consequences.

axioms.title: Attention and time remain radically scarce
axioms.rule: Abundant intelligence and content increase the importance of deciding what deserves attention.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Train attention, curation, priority, refusal, deep reading, long projects and deliberate practice.

axioms.title: Judgment is selection under plural constraints
axioms.rule: Competence is not merely producing valid options but choosing among them under uncertainty, values, tradeoffs and consequences.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Use comparison, decision records, forecasting, multi-criteria design, ethics, taste and viva defense.

axioms.title: Taste is a serious faculty of educated discrimination
axioms.rule: When competent outputs become abundant, quality selection, coherence, fittingness, originality, elegance and humane restraint become more important.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Train taste across proof, prose, science, software, design, institutions, art and ways of life through exemplars, making, critique and revision.

axioms.title: Agency is practiced, not downloaded
axioms.rule: Knowing what to do does not create the capacity to initiate, persist, coordinate, repair and take responsibility.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Use long projects, craft, service, leadership, household operation, civic participation and real stakeholder work.

axioms.title: Humans are embodied and vulnerable
axioms.rule: Health, movement, sleep, care, mortality, place, tools and physical constraints remain constitutive of human life even in digital abundance.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Protect health literacy, physical practice, care, repair, emergency readiness, nature/place and embodied skill.

axioms.title: Humans are relational and political
axioms.rule: People become capable through families, teachers, peers, institutions, traditions and communities; power shapes available choices.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Teach relationships, dialogue, consent, negotiation, institutions, law, markets, power, history and public agency.

axioms.title: Culture is an inheritance and a living creation
axioms.rule: A civilization that can generate infinite new content can still lose memory, standards, tradition and historical consciousness.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Preserve whole works, civilizational anchors, arts, religions, philosophies, history, languages and creative practice in a revisable canon.

axioms.title: Tools amplify both wisdom and error
axioms.rule: More capable AI increases the upside of good objectives and the downside of confused objectives, weak institutions or miscalibrated trust.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Make AI stewardship, evals, permissions, provenance, monitoring, fallback and governance universal.

axioms.title: Institutions matter more as systems exceed individuals
axioms.rule: When no person can fully audit a system, assurance must become social and institutional rather than purely individual.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Teach independent evaluation, competing systems, checks and balances, audits, recourse, dissent, stop-work authority and reversible deployment.

axioms.title: A good life is plural but not contentless
axioms.rule: Education should not dictate one life plan, yet it can cultivate capacities that support many worthwhile lives.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Teach reflective commitment, practical independence, relationships, health, culture, civic agency and the ability to revise one's purposes.

axioms.title: Education must survive technological regime change
axioms.rule: The curriculum should remain valuable if model architectures, vendors, labor markets or AGI timelines differ radically from current expectations.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Keep volatile tools in replaceable labs and durable concepts, practices and responsibilities in the core.

axioms.title: Formation links past, present and future
axioms.rule: Education transmits hard-won human knowledge while preparing learners to revise it and steward what comes next.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Pair historical inheritance with contemporary science and future-oriented institutional/technological judgment.

axioms.title: Mastery is multi-dimensional
axioms.rule: No single test score, degree or artifact captures broad human competence.
axioms.curriculum_consequence: Maintain separate evidence for knowledge, models, transfer, practice, judgment, communication, AI stewardship, reality contact, responsibility, learning autonomy and stewardship.

eight_verbs.meaning: Receive the strongest available human knowledge, works, methods, traditions and lessons without becoming captive to them.
Build internal models of reality, mechanism, history, mind, society and technology from first principles where possible.
Discriminate truth, quality, value, risk and tradeoffs under uncertainty.
Make explanations, arguments, designs, systems, art, institutions and culture with craft and taste.
Initiate, execute, persist, coordinate, repair and accept responsibility in the real world.
Listen, care, love, negotiate, teach, collaborate, belong and preserve the agency of others.
Use power responsibly across institutions, technology, culture, nature and generations.
Continue learning, updating and reforming one's models and practices as the world changes.
